blinding_guess.why: driver.py and prog are mutually consistent (message codes 1-14, integer word counts for MSG_SERVOJ/MSG_SET_PAYLOAD/MSG_SET_DIGITAL_OUT match between sender and reader, MULT_* scalings identical). Whether the URScript calls (servoj(q, 0, 0, dt), set_payload(payload) with no CoG, movej(q, a, v, t, r)) and the fixed packet lengths assumed for ports 30002/30003 (RobotStateRT 756/812/1044, RobotModeData 29/38, MasterboardData 64/76/72/92) match a given controller software version cannot be judged from the snapshot; unknown lengths fall through to empty objects whose attribute access would fail.

notes: No packet element is a ROS topic/service/message, so msg_type, definition_id, units and qos are null for every port (ROS 1, and the elements are URScript functions or TCP ports of the robot controller). api:driverProg is the URScript program defined in ur_driver/prog (line 1, invoked at line 229); driver.py reads the file, fills %(driver_hostname)s and %(driver_reverseport)d, and sends it to the controller over port 30002 (driver.py:953-958, 158). Frame is null for api:driverProg, api:movej and api:servoj: they carry joint-space positions (q, divided by MULT_jointstate) and no coordinate frame is declared; null for the two TCP resources, whose streams mix joint and Cartesian data without a frame named in code. The movej call (prog:144) sits in the MSG_MOVEJ branch; driver.py defines MSG_MOVEJ = 4 but has no method that sends it (the only other movej occurrence is commented out at prog:96). servoj is called from servoThread (prog:81) with the setpoint written by MSG_SERVOJ (prog:147-167); driver.py sends MSG_SERVOJ every RATE = 0.02 s with t = 4 * RATE (driver.py:659, 678, 800), but no rate is set on the servoj call itself, so rate_hz is null. Ports 30002 and 30003 are consumed as TCP clients (socket.create_connection, driver.py:145, 308); comments state 10 Hz and 125 Hz controller send rates (driver.py:39-40; ur_msgs msg comments), which are rates of the peer, not set by this code, so rate_hz is null. The driver also binds a listening TCPServer on reverse_port (default DEFAULT_REVERSE_PORT = 50001, allow_reuse_address = True, driver.py:41, 545, 948); this is a local listening socket, not recorded as an exclusive hardware resource. prog also calls URScript builtins outside the packet (socket_send_string, stopj, set_flag, set_analog_out, set_tool_voltage, sync, enter_critical/exit_critical); these are not listed in references, which is restricted to packet elements. resource: names are not in the canonical-name list of the prompt; they are recorded in references under the packet's own element names. Recovery recorded as present is code behaviour (reconnect-and-reprogram loop, driver.py:975-992); the URConnection/URConnectionRT socket threads themselves only mark DISCONNECTED and do not reconnect (driver.py:179-181, 281-286, 325-327, 378-383).
